key_insight: MMFlash studies faster speculative decoding for vision-language models, focusing on how much generated tokens depend on visual input. It introduces a token-level metric to quantify that dependence.
problem_solved: Diffusion-based drafting can propose whole token blocks efficiently, but existing work mainly addresses text-only tasks, leaving image-conditioned generation underexplored.
method: Study multimodal speculative decoding, where a lightweight drafter proposes tokens for parallel verification by a target model.
Measure token-level visual dependence using KL divergence between next-token distributions with and without visual input.
Investigate this setting in the context of diffusion drafters, which propose an entire token block in one forward pass.
impact: Understanding visual dependence could help practitioners design faster drafting strategies for vision-language models. The supplied abstract is truncated, so MMFlash’s full design, findings, and speedups cannot be confirmed.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: image and prompt → draft token block → target-model verification.
Paired next-token distributions with and without an image, highlighting their KL divergence.
Conceptual token heatmap showing low versus high visual dependence.
Side-by-side schematic of sequential token generation and single-pass block drafting.
paper_title: MMFlash: Faster Speculative Decoding for Vision-Language Models
paper_authors: Sicheng Feng, Zigeng Chen, Song Wang, Gongfan Fang, Xinchao Wang
